hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with altered mental status, fever (or hypothermia), tachycardia, tachypnea, and hypotension unresponsive to fluid resuscitation — requiring vasopressors to maintain MAP ≥65. Lactate is elevated (>2 mmol/L) indicating tissue hypoperfusion. Sepsis = SIRS + infection. Septic shock = sepsis + persistent hypotension despite fluids + lactate >2. Source must be identified: blood cultures x2, urine culture, CXR, and cultures from any suspected site (sputum, wound, CSF). Empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 HOUR of recognition — every hour delay increases mortality 7-8%. Initial resuscitation: 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid bolus. If still hypotensive → start vasopressors (norepinephrine first-line). Monitor lactate clearance (goal >20% decrease). Measure ScvO2. Admit to ICU. Source control: remove lines, drain abscess, debridement if needed.
